## Flagship Research Monograph 1: The 3DS Oracle
- **Title**: The 3DS Oracle: BIN Attack via the Network
- **Identifier**: arXiv:2610.32206 [cs.CR] (October 2026)
- **Authors**: Wasif Faisal (Lead Researcher), Suprava Saha Dibya
- **Paper Link**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32206
- **PDF Link**: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32206
- **Full Security Disclosure**: https://cswasif.github.io/blog/2026/security-disclosure-the-3ds-oracle-and-the-tragedy-of-the-payment-commons/

### Technical Summary & Core Findings:
1. **Systemic Architectural Flaw**: In browser-mediated 3-D Secure 2.x (3DS) authentication flows, client-visible continuation boundaries can expose a pre-authorization authentication classification channel (an "oracle").
2. **Circular Trust Boundary**: The 3DS specification formally treats the merchant requestor environment as out-of-scope of its security boundary, while issuers and Directory Servers (DS) simultaneously make risk and continuation routing decisions based on client-supplied data before financial authorization ever begins.
3. **Three In-The-Wild Abuse Patterns**:
   - *Card-Number Harvesting*: Off-context callers reverse-engineer response differentials to construct and harvest valid card numbers off-context.
   - *Pre-Authorization Screening*: Threat actors filter stolen card dumps prior to financial authorization, bypassing downstream zero-dollar authorization filters.
   - *Bank-Profiling & Internal Routing Inference*: Differences in authentication continuation signals leak bank-internal segmentation and routing rules across BIN ranges.
4. **Failure of Reactive Defenses & Patent Prosecution Confirmation**:
   - Payment networks attempted downstream velocity scoring (e.g., Mastercard patent application US 2026/0134429 A1, Conroy et al.).
   - On August 25, 2026, the USPTO rejected all 20 claims under 35 U.S.C. § 101 (unpatentable abstract idea) and § 102/103 (anticipated by earlier Thomson patent US 2022/0108331 A1 and obvious).
   - Downstream velocity heuristics fail because attackers rotate residential proxy pools and spoof browser telemetry; statistical filtering cannot remedy an architectural confidentiality leak.

---

## Research Monograph 2: Card Reissuance Prefix Limits
- **Title**: Prefix Count Limits Can Increase First-Hit Discovery in Card Reissuance
- **Identifier**: arXiv:2609.31398 [cs.CR] (September 2026)
- **Author**: Wasif Faisal
- **Paper Link**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31398
- **PDF Link**: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.31398

### Technical Summary:
- Investigates the statistical and security properties of card reissuance numbering policies.
- Evaluates 50,000 synthetic card candidates to demonstrate that imposing strict prefix count limits can counterintuitively increase first-hit discovery probability for adversaries executing automated BIN enumeration attacks.
- Provides actionable reissuance risk assessment frameworks for banking institutions and card issuers.
